## Summary

- The Operations group adds a read-only host screen. It opens on the last 24 hours and can switch to the last hour or to the samples the store still holds. The screen shows CPU, memory, swap, filesystems, disk, pressure, Postgres connections, checkpoints, and temporary files, plus CPU time and memory for the eight site services. It records the numbers and does not apply a threshold. `host:read` is required.
- Model Services use one embedding call for Catalog and Entity. A service record carries `batch_limit` (1–32, default 32). Purpose state reports `catalog_index` and `entity_index` separately. `ready` and `index_status` on the purpose object remain the Catalog index.
- Entity MCP adds `search_entities`. It ranks serving Entities the caller can read by cosine similarity of definition text. The call needs an open in-use embedding service and an Entity index that is ready on that generation. It does not write rows, produce SQL, or fall back to a name search. The existing seven tools keep their arguments and results.
- The site schedule `entity_embed:site` rebuilds the Entity definition index. Its seeded cron is `0 3 * * *`. Catalog embedding stays on its own schedule. Activating a service, or changing an in-use URL or model, clears both indexes and runs both schedules.
- Console breadcrumbs stay a two-segment trail, including alias paths for actions that are not the list.

## Operator notes

- Upgrade from v0.7.0. v0.1.6 and v0.1.9 were tagged and are not installable. Do not install them.
- Add `REFRAQ_MONITOR_PASSWORD` to the live `.env` before starting this compose. It is the password for login `refraq_monitor` (`LOGIN`, `NOSUPERUSER`, granted `pg_monitor`). Use URL-safe characters only (no `@`, `:`, `/`, `%`, `?`, or `#`). `docker compose` refuses to start until the key is set. `REFRAQ_PROMETHEUS_URL` is optional and defaults to `http://prometheus:9090`. Leave the rest of the live `.env` in place.
- Download `docker-compose.yaml` and `prometheus.yml` from this release and overwrite both. Replacing only the Compose file leaves Prometheus without a scrape file. Do not overwrite the live `.env`.
- Compose still mounts named volume `refraq_pg` at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Default PGDATA is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. A site already on that mount keeps its cluster. A site that only used the published v0.1.8 asset must still copy the anonymous-volume cluster onto `refraq_pg` before `up -d`, using the command in the v0.1.10 notes. Do not run `docker compose down -v`. Do not restore `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
- This compose adds `node-exporter`, `cadvisor`, `ensure-monitor-role`, `postgres-exporter`, and `prometheus`. Prometheus stores samples on the new named volume `refraq_prometheus` for `15d` or `1073741824` bytes, whichever comes first. `node-exporter` uses the host network and listens on host port `9100`. Block `9100` from everything except the Compose bridge. The Compose file does not publish that port and does not enforce the firewall rule. `cadvisor` is privileged and limited to the eight Compose services. Postgres keeps blkio weight 500 and Prometheus uses 100. A weight is a relative preference under contention, not a latency guarantee.
- Replace the files, then `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The new image tag recreates `ensure-entity-db` (`restart: "no"`). That one-shot still prepares `entity_data`, `entity_access`, `acl`, `channel_dataset`, and `entity_change_log`. It does not delete Entity rows. `ensure-monitor-role` (`restart: "no"`) creates `refraq_monitor` when missing, then aligns the password and grants `pg_monitor`. api and worker still refuse to start while any of those five schemas is missing. Worker and Beat stay on the api image tag.
- API start runs Foundation Upgrade `0087_model_service_shared_controls` through `0090_entity_index_state`. `0087` widens `alembic_version.version_num` to `varchar(64)`, then sets existing services to `batch_limit` 32 and existing embedding purpose rows to `control_revision` 0 and processing contract `prefix-1024-l2-v1`. It does not advance `generation`. `0088` creates empty `entity_embeddings`. `0089` copies the existing purpose ready bit into `catalog_index_state` and does not enqueue a Catalog rebuild. `0090` inserts `entity_index_state` with `ready` false and does not enqueue a refill. None of these revisions delete tokens, catalog rows, Entity rows, channel rows, run records, or Catalog embedding rows.
- API start seeds schedule key `entity_embed:site` when that row is missing: enabled, undeletable, cron `0 3 * * *`, evaluated in `schedule_timezone` (the parameter seed is UTC). An existing row keeps its cadence. Startup does not mint an `entity_embed` Job. Until a sweep publishes, Entity MCP `search_entities` fails with `ENTITY_INDEX_NOT_READY`. Run that schedule from its row when the index should exist before the next cron tick. A Catalog index that was ready stays ready, and Catalog Search keeps reading that bit.
- `host:read` is in the Permission catalog and in the effective permissions of `super_admin`. It is not seeded onto `operator`. Foundation Upgrade does not rewrite stored permission lists, so an existing custom Role does not receive the key until it is granted. Without it, the host screen is absent and `GET /host` is `403` `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`. A Session or a User PAT with the key can read. An omitted `span` is `day`. `hour`, `day`, and `retained` are the only values. Any other value is `422` `REQUEST_INVALID`. An unreachable series store is `503` `HOST_SERIES_UNAVAILABLE`, not a payload of zeros.
- `GET /model-services` records add `batch_limit`. `GET /model-services/purpose/embedding` adds `control_revision`, `catalog_index`, and `entity_index`. `ready` equals `catalog_index.ready`. Create may omit `batch_limit` and then stores 32. An in-use URL or model change, activate, and force-generation clear both ready bits, increment `generation` and `control_revision`, and run both site schedules. Close keeps both vector stores, makes Catalog Search lexical, and refuses Entity semantic search. Cleanup, when the purpose is closed or has no in-use service, deletes Catalog embedding rows and Entity projection rows. A non-terminal `catalog_embed` or `entity_embed` Job makes cleanup `MODEL_SERVICE_CLEANUP_BUSY`.
- Metadata MCP tool arguments and tool-call results are unchanged. Entity MCP `tools/list` adds `search_entities` with `execution` `read`. The previous seven tools are unchanged. `search_entities` takes `query_text` and an optional `limit` from 1 through 50. No in-use service is `MODEL_SERVICE_NOT_IN_USE`. A closed purpose is `MODEL_SERVICE_CLOSED`. A missing URL is `MODEL_SERVICE_ENDPOINT_MISSING`. A failed query embed is `ENTITY_SEARCH_EMBED_FAILED`. The tool writes no Entity Access Log record. Webhook delivery is unchanged.
- Rolling back to an older compose after this migration is not supported. Downgrade of `0090` drops `entity_index_state`. Downgrade of `0089` drops `catalog_index_state`. Downgrade of `0088` drops `entity_embeddings`. Downgrade of `0087` drops `batch_limit`, `control_revision`, and `processing_contract`, and leaves `alembic_version.version_num` as `varchar(64)`.
